topicName: Debugging and Profiling (PyTorch Profiler, Kineto, NaN traps)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Debugging and Profiling in PyTorch"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deep learning models are notoriously difficult to debug due to their asynchronous execution, complex graph structures, and the black-box nature of GPU training. This tutorial covers advanced techniques for diagnosing performance bottlenecks and numerical instability using the PyTorch Profiler, Kineto, and NaN traps."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Numerical Stability and NaN Traps"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"NaN (Not a Number) values usually stem from division by zero, log of zero, or exploding gradients in mixed-precision training. PyTorch provides built-in context managers to detect these anomalies instantly by breaking execution right where the invalid value is generated."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch

torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True)

x = torch.randn(3, 3, requires_grad=True)
weight = torch.zeros(3, 3, requires_grad=True)

# Simulating a division by zero or invalid log operation
out = x / weight
loss = out.sum()

try:
    loss.backward()
except Exception as e:
    print("Anomaly detected:", e)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Performance Profiling with PyTorch Profiler and Kineto"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"PyTorch integrates directly with Kineto, an open-source library that traces CPU and GPU operations, including kernel execution times, memory allocations, and host-device interactions. The profiler context manager allows targeted profiling of training steps."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torchvision.models as models

model = models.resnet18().cuda()
inputs = torch.randn(16, 3, 224, 224).cuda()
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)

with torch.profiler.profile(
    activities=[
        torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU,
        torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA,
    ],
    schedule=torch.profiler.schedule(wait=1, warmup=1, active=3, repeat=1),
    on_trace_ready=torch.profiler.tensorboard_trace_handler("./log/resnet18"),
    record_shapes=True,
    profile_memory=True,
    with_stack=True
) as prof:
    for step in range(5):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        outputs = model(inputs)
        loss = outputs.sum()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        prof.step()"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Analyzing Memory Bottlenecks"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Memory fragmentation and out-of-memory (OOM) errors are common during deep learning training. You can track memory allocation snapshots using PyTorch memory history features."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Enable memory history recording to diagnose OOM issues
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(max_entries=100000)

# Run your memory-intensive code here...

# Export the snapshot to visualize in the PyTorch memory viz tool
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("memory_snapshot.pickle")
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(None)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Profiling"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always include a warmup phase (e.g., 1-2 steps) in the profiler schedule to avoid compilation and CUDA context initialization overheads skewing the results."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use with_stack=True judiciously, as tracking Python call stacks introduces noticeable performance overhead during execution."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Export traces to TensorBoard or the Chrome Tracing tool (chrome://tracing or ui.perfetto.dev) for granular visualization of timeline events."}]
